sources.name: EDHREC closing diff (DEC-402), 2026-08-20, revision 2
sources.detail: Diffed the final 99 against the EDHREC top cards and each deck-relevant category. Fourteen cards sit at 40 percent inclusion or above and are not in this list. Triage. REJECT Cavern-Hoard Dragon (nine mana, reduced only by the greatest artifact count one opponent controls, so it usually still costs five to seven). REJECT Magda, Brazen Outlaw (her trigger needs a Dwarf to become tapped; the deck runs zero Dwarves). REJECT Alchemist's Talent (level 3 costs eleven mana in total before it deals any damage). REJECT Generous Plunderer (its upkeep trigger gives an opponent a Treasure as well). REJECT Dragon-Cursed Halls (colorless-only land against 36 black and 29 red pips). REJECT Smaug the Impenetrable (seven mana, and its Treasure trigger needs noncombat damage dealt to itself, which this deck cannot arrange). REJECT Descent into Avernus (symmetric — it ramps three opponents to accelerate us once). REJECT Desolation of Smaug (three damage to each non-Dragon creature kills most of our own payoffs). REJECT Haunted Ridge and Blazemire Verge (both cost real money and the free-pool manabase already scores 83). DEFER Rain of Riches (cut late for the two tutors; note its cascade does not spend Treasure mana, so it never triggers Smaug). DEFER Grim Hireling, The Reaver Cleaver and Ancient Copper Dragon (all three are strong but combat-gated, and this deck does not attack reliably). REVISION 2, after the board-approved round-2 swaps. Rain of Riches moves from DEFER to INCLUDE at 65.7 percent: its cascade clause and Smaug's draw clause share the same trigger condition, which is that Treasure mana paid for the spell. Four cards cut this round re-enter the diff above the 40 percent bar and are rejected on the record. REJECT Smaug the Magnificent at 74.3 percent: its damage is attack-gated, so it fires once per turn cycle and only when we attack. REJECT Nadier's Nightblade at 45.9 percent: it drains only when a token leaves, while Mirkwood Bats drains when a token is created or sacrificed, which is strictly more frequent here. REJECT Terminate at 45.6 percent: the deck keeps nine other spot answers plus Vandalblast and three sweepers. REJECT Dark Ritual at 44.3 percent: a one-shot ritual is dead after turn four against 38 lands, six rocks and heavy Treasure output. Seize the Spoils at 38.1 percent sits below the bar and needs no line. Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer at 33.8 percent also sits below the bar; the board asked about it, and it is rejected for the same attack-gated reason as Smaug the Magnificent. Ragavan is not on the official Game Changers list, so this rejection is not a bracket decision.

sources.name: Board round-2 swap approval, DEC-543, 2026-08-20
sources.detail: Board accepted all five swaps. IN Vandalblast, Warren Soultrader, Umbral Collar Zealot, Rain of Riches, Fountainport. OUT Smaug the Magnificent, Nadier's Nightblade, Terminate, Dark Ritual, Seize the Spoils. Board also rejected Knuckles the Echidna: its win clause needs thirty artifacts, while Hellkite Tyrant already wins at twenty and Revel in Riches at ten Treasures. Board approved the two purchases, Warren Soultrader second copy at $14.04 and Rain of Riches at $4.38.

sources.name: Board round-4 swap approval, DEC-543, 2026-08-20
sources.detail: Board approved The Mycosynth Gardens over Temple of Malice, and approved Oni-Cult Anvil on the condition that a card the deck does not need comes out. The cut is Yawgmoth, Thran Physician. Yawgmoth needs another creature for every activation, and the deck's only repeatable creature fodder is Reassembling Skeleton at {1}{B} per return, so each Yawgmoth card costs {1}{B} plus 1 life. Skullclamp draws two off the same Skeleton for three mana and no life. Oni-Cult Anvil sacrifices an artifact instead, which is the resource this deck makes in bulk, and it returns 1 life per activation.

sources.name: Board round-5 and round-6 swap approvals, DEC-543, 2026-08-20
sources.detail: Round 5, interaction 233b34ef: board chose option ophio_abrade. IN Ophiomancer, OUT Abrade. Board also kept Goblin Bombardment, which is one of only two free, instant-speed, no-life sacrifice outlets and the enabler that turns Ophiomancer into up to four Snakes per turn cycle. Round 6, interaction f2d9842b: board approved Bloodghast IN and Umbral Collar Zealot OUT, then reversed the round-5 removal choice and asked for Abrade back over Bedevil. Bloodghast is the cheapest Skullclamp target in the deck, at {1} per two cards against three mana for the same two off Reassembling Skeleton, and it survives the deck's own three sweepers. Umbral Collar Zealot was the cut because its payoff per activation is Surveil 1, the weakest of any outlet here, its creature-or-artifact flexibility is already covered by Ashnod's Altar, Goblin Bombardment and Krark-Clan Ironworks, and it appears in none of the five Spellbook combos. Cuts rejected on the record: Blasphemous Act and Spiteful Banditry each open a removal-board gap; Black Market Connections and Braids each open a card-draw gap; Chaos Warp and Feed the Swarm are the only two answers to an enchantment; Marionette Apprentice and Crime Novelist are payoffs that Bloodghast's own death triggers. Abrade over Bedevil keeps the artifact-answer count at three (Abrade, Chaos Warp, Vandalblast) and drops the cost from {B}{B}{R} to {1}{R}. It gives up Bedevil's reach onto planeswalkers, which leaves Chaos Warp as the only card in the 99 that answers one, and it downgrades creature removal from destroy-anything to three damage.

sources.name: Board round-7 swap approval and wincon retag, DEC-543, 2026-08-21
sources.detail: Round 7, interaction edf19f77. Board chose option wt_grasp: IN Withering Torment, OUT Infernal Grasp. Both are instants that destroy a creature and cost the caster 2 life; Withering Torment costs one more mana and adds an enchantment mode. That takes enchantment answers from two to three, which matters because Rest in Peace alone stops Reassembling Skeleton, Bloodghast and Reanimate. The spot-answer count stays at eight. Board also chose option retag on wincon_style. The deck-level tag moves from combo to drain. Basis: the goldfish simulation puts the damage proxy at 46.9 percent by turn 7 against 5.1 percent for combo lethal, so incremental life loss is the dominant plan and the combo is the ceiling, not the clock. The retag is not cosmetic. It raises the resilience recursion target from 2 to 3 (RESILIENCE_RECURSION_TARGETS, combo versus drain at bracket 4), which cuts resilience_health from 94 to 84, global_health from 96 to 95, and opens one recursion gap at 2.0 of 3. The win-turn triple does not move: multi-kind detection already drove it off max(comboLethal, lethalProxy) under both tags.

guideContent.strategyOverview:
Smaug, Wicked Worm turns Treasures into cards. Its second ability reads "Whenever you cast a spell, if mana from a Treasure was spent to cast it, you draw a card and lose 1 life." The trigger fires once per spell, not once per Treasure. That single fact sets the whole build: the deck wants many cheap spells, not a few expensive ones. The average mana value of the 59 nonland cards is 2.92.

Smaug draws cards. It does not win. This deck supplies the kill in three layers.

Layer one is incidental damage. A Treasure pays twice in this list. It deals damage when it enters, through Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent. It drains when it is sacrificed, through Marionette Apprentice, Marionette Master, Mirkwood Bats and Mayhem Devil. Xorn and Academy Manufactor multiply the entering half, so the damage curve is steeply nonlinear rather than incremental.

Layer two is the deterministic loop. Pitiless Plunderer plus Ashnod's Altar plus Reassembling Skeleton produces infinite colorless mana and infinite death triggers. Four different payoffs already in the deck convert that loop into a kill, so no single removal spell stops it.

Layer three is the alternate win. Revel in Riches wins at ten Treasures. Hellkite Tyrant wins at twenty artifacts at our upkeep, and Mycosynth Lattice makes every permanent an artifact, so the check counts our whole board once both are on the battlefield.

The cost of Smaug's trigger is real, and one card reverses it. Smaug charges one life per Treasure-cast spell and the trigger is not optional. Warren Soultrader, Black Market Connections, Grim Tutor, Reanimate, Withering Torment, Feed the Swarm, Phyrexian Reclamation and six painful lands all charge life on top. The usual aristocrats life buffer is unavailable here on purpose: Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance all trigger on creature death only and never fire on a sacrificed Treasure, which is what this deck actually sacrifices. Sheoldred, the Apocalypse is the answer this color pair does allow. She reads "Whenever you draw a card, you gain 2 life", and Smaug's trigger is a draw, so every Treasure-cast spell swings from minus one life to plus one. Without her, Exsanguinate, High Market and Oni-Cult Anvil are the only cards that give life back and none is cheap or repeatable, so the deck plays as a short-clock deck that must convert its board before its own life total becomes the shortest at the table. With her, the same list can grind.

categories.name: Treasure Engines
categories.description: Repeatable Treasure production. These cards feed Smaug's cast trigger, the sacrifice payoffs and the mana base at the same time. Warren Soultrader converts a creature straight into an artifact for one life. Rain of Riches adds cascade to the first spell each turn that Treasure mana paid for, which is the same condition Smaug already rewards. Storm-Kiln Artist makes a Treasure on every instant or sorcery we cast or copy, and the deck runs twenty-one of them.

categories.name: Token Multipliers
categories.description: Replacement effects that turn one Treasure instruction into several tokens. They multiply the entering-damage half of the plan, not just the mana.

categories.name: Sacrifice Outlets
categories.description: Free or near-free outlets that convert permanents into triggers. Ashnod's Altar and Krark-Clan Ironworks also add mana, which is what makes the loop work. Read this list by fodder type. Krark-Clan Ironworks and Oni-Cult Anvil eat an artifact, which is what this deck produces in bulk; every Treasure also sacrifices itself for mana, so the deck is never short of a way to move an artifact to the graveyard. Ashnod's Altar, Goblin Bombardment, Warren Soultrader and High Market need a creature instead. See Sacrifice Fodder for what feeds that half.

categories.name: Sacrifice Fodder
categories.description: Bodies for the creature-fed outlets. Ophiomancer triggers at the beginning of each upkeep, so it makes a 1/1 deathtouch Snake on all four turns of a four-player cycle, provided a free outlet eats the Snake before the next upkeep — that is what Goblin Bombardment and Ashnod's Altar are for. Bloodghast returns itself for free on every land drop, which makes it the cheapest Skullclamp target in the deck: {1} to equip draws two cards, against three mana for the same two off Reassembling Skeleton. It also survives our own Blasphemous Act, Toxic Deluge and Spiteful Banditry, which Ophiomancer does not. Note that Bloodghast is not a token, so it never triggers Mirkwood Bats or The Sackville-Bagginses directly; it reaches them through the Treasure that Pitiless Plunderer banks on its death. Reassembling Skeleton returns for {1}{B} as often as mana allows. Marionette Apprentice and Marionette Master each make tokens once, and only if you decline their +1/+1 counters. Black Market Connections makes a 3/2 for 3 life, which this deck's life total rarely wants to pay.

categories.name: Drain and Damage Payoffs
categories.description: Every card here fires on artifact or token movement, not on creature death. That gating is the single correction that separates this list from a generic aristocrats build.

categories.name: Rituals and Fast Mana
categories.description: Cheap acceleration that lets the deck deploy two spells in a turn. Every extra spell cast off Treasure mana is an extra card from Smaug.

categories.name: Card Advantage
categories.description: Draw that does not depend on Smaug being on the battlefield, plus the card that makes Smaug's draw free. Skullclamp is the engine here: equip it to Reassembling Skeleton for {1}, the Skeleton dies, we draw two, and it returns from the graveyard for {1}{B}. That is three mana for two cards, repeatable, and Pitiless Plunderer turns each of those deaths into a Treasure. Sheoldred, the Apocalypse reads "Whenever you draw a card, you gain 2 life", so it cancels the life Smaug charges and leaves one life over on every Treasure-cast spell.

categories.name: Tutors
categories.description: Four tutors, none of them a Game Changer. Diabolic Intent sacrifices a creature we were going to sacrifice anyway. Beseech the Mirror is the best of the four here: bargain by sacrificing a Treasure, then cast the found card for free if its mana value is 4 or less. Ashnod's Altar, Pitiless Plunderer and Krark-Clan Ironworks all clear that bar, so one Beseech assembles a third of the combo and deploys it in the same turn.

categories.name: Interaction
categories.description: Eight spot answers plus Vandalblast and three sweepers. Deadly Rollick and Deflecting Swat are the free spells that Bracket 4 asks for in black and red. Withering Torment, Feed the Swarm and Chaos Warp are the three answers to an enchantment, which matters because Rest in Peace turns off Reassembling Skeleton, Bloodghast and Reanimate at once, and because Stony Silence shuts off every Treasure we make. Abrade, Chaos Warp and Vandalblast are the three answers to an artifact, which is what a resolved Grafdigger's Cage or Torpor Orb needs. Vandalblast answers an artifact for one mana and wipes every artifact we do not control for {4}{R}. Chaos Warp is the only card here that answers a planeswalker, so hold it for one rather than spending it on a creature.

categories.name: Protection and Recursion
categories.description: Insurance against a board wipe, which is this deck's worst matchup because all eight of the drain and damage payoffs are creatures. Phyrexian Reclamation is the only piece that rebuys a payoff more than once: {1}{B} and 2 life returns any creature card from the graveyard to hand, as often as mana allows. With Sheoldred on the battlefield a single Smaug draw pays that 2 life back.

categories.name: Mana Base
categories.description: Thirty-eight lands. Great Furnace and Vault of Whispers are artifact lands, so they trigger the artifacts-entering payoffs and count toward Hellkite Tyrant. High Market is a free sacrifice outlet on a land. Fountainport makes a Treasure for {4} and turns a spare token into a card for {2}, both without using the stack for a spell. Mines of Moria enters untapped whenever Smaug or another legendary creature is out. The Mycosynth Gardens enters untapped, and for {X} and a tap it becomes a copy of a nontoken artifact we control with mana value X. Copying Academy Manufactor for {3} is the reason it is here; two Manufactors turn one Treasure instruction into three Clues, three Foods and three Treasures.

winConditions.title: Infinite loop into a drain payoff
winConditions.description: Sacrifice Reassembling Skeleton to Ashnod's Altar. The Altar adds two colorless mana and Pitiless Plunderer creates a Treasure. Return the Skeleton for one generic and one black, paying with one colorless plus the Treasure. One colorless mana is left over, so the loop is mana-positive and repeats without limit. It produces infinite death triggers and infinite Treasure creations. Four payoffs already in the deck convert that into a kill, so removing any one of them does not stop it. Confirmed by Commander Spellbook combo 1580-2034-4871.

winConditions.title: Treasure storm — entering damage plus sacrifice drain
winConditions.description: One Treasure instruction with Xorn and Academy Manufactor both on the battlefield creates six tokens. Ordering matters: apply Xorn first, so one Treasure becomes two, then Academy Manufactor turns that into two Clues, two Foods and two Treasures. CR 616.1 lets us choose that order. All six are artifacts. With Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent also out, each fires six times for one, so that is twelve damage to each opponent. Mirkwood Bats adds six more as life loss, not damage, because it reads "Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses 1 life." Eighteen life leaves each opponent in total. State the basis plainly: that number needs five specific permanents. With only Fireweaver and Bats it is two to each opponent. This line is nonlinear, not incremental.

winConditions.title: Alternate win — Revel in Riches or Hellkite Tyrant
winConditions.description: Revel in Riches wins at the beginning of our upkeep with ten or more Treasures. Treasure Vault, Xorn and Academy Manufactor make that count reachable in one turn. Hellkite Tyrant wins at the beginning of our upkeep with twenty or more artifacts. Mycosynth Lattice makes every permanent an artifact, so the check counts our whole board, not just our artifacts: with ten lands, Lattice, Hellkite and a few creatures we are close, and one Treasure instruction under Xorn and Academy Manufactor covers the rest. Both checks happen at our upkeep, which gives the table a full turn cycle to answer them. Treat them as backup, not as the plan.

winConditions.title: Exsanguinate off infinite mana
winConditions.description: The loop in win condition one makes unbounded colorless mana. Exsanguinate converts it directly, draining each opponent for X and gaining that much life. This is the clean out when every drain payoff has been removed but the loop pieces survive.

synergies.title: A Treasure pays twice
synergies.description: Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent both trigger when an artifact we control enters. Marionette Apprentice and Marionette Master trigger when an artifact we control is put into a graveyard. Mirkwood Bats covers both halves, because it reads "Whenever you create or sacrifice a token." So the same Treasure deals damage on the way in and drains on the way out. Weftstalker Ardent is the widest of the four: it reads "another creature or artifact you control", so it also fires on Ophiomancer's Snakes, on every Bloodghast return and on anything we reanimate.

sources.name: Board-supplied Moxfield list
sources.detail: The entering-damage package came from this list. Revision 1 of the analysis had valued Treasures as sacrifice fodder only.

synergies.title: Xorn plus Academy Manufactor — replacement ordering
synergies.description: Both are replacement effects that apply to the same token-creation event, so CR 616.1 lets us choose the order. Apply Xorn first and one Treasure becomes two; Academy Manufactor then turns that into two Clues, two Foods and two Treasures, for six tokens. The reverse order yields four. The per-card texts and the Manufactor multiplication are printed rules; the choice of order is ours.

sources.name: Scryfall ruling on Academy Manufactor
sources.detail: "If you control one Academy Manufactor and would create some number of Clue, Food, or Treasure tokens, you will instead create that many Clue tokens, that many Food tokens, and that many Treasure tokens."

synergies.title: Crime Novelist and Krark-Clan Ironworks price a Treasure at three mana
synergies.description: Krark-Clan Ironworks reads "Sacrifice an artifact: Add two colorless mana." Crime Novelist reads "Whenever you sacrifice an artifact, put a plus-one plus-one counter on this creature and add one red mana." Sacrificing one Treasure through Ironworks with Crime Novelist out yields three mana, where the Treasure alone would have yielded one. Same inputs, three times the output.

sources.name: CEO derivation
sources.detail: Both oracle texts verified on Scryfall 2026-08-20. Arithmetic is ours.

synergies.title: Artifact lands are free payoff triggers
synergies.description: Great Furnace, Vault of Whispers and Treasure Vault are artifact lands. Playing one triggers Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent, counts toward Hellkite Tyrant's twenty artifacts, and can be sacrificed to Krark-Clan Ironworks for two mana. They cost the deck nothing over a basic land except vulnerability to artifact sweepers.

sources.name: CEO analysis
sources.detail: Type lines verified on Scryfall 2026-08-20.

synergies.title: Mycosynth Lattice widens Marionette Master and Hellkite Tyrant
synergies.description: Mycosynth Lattice reads "All permanents are artifacts in addition to their other types." With it out, every permanent we lose is an artifact hitting the graveyard, so Marionette Master triggers on our creature and land deaths too, and every land we play triggers Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent. It also makes Hellkite Tyrant's twenty-artifact upkeep check count our whole board. Know the limit of the Lattice plus overloaded Vandalblast line: it destroys every permanent our opponents control, but nothing in the 99 drains off that. Marionette Master reads "an artifact you control", so it does not fire on their permanents. Vandalblast under Lattice is a one-sided board wipe, and Hellkite Tyrant is the card that turns the aftermath into a win. The cost is symmetry: our own board becomes vulnerable to any artifact sweeper.

sources.name: Mycosynth Lattice + Hellkite Tyrant
sources.detail: Listed as a two-card win.

synergies.title: Sheoldred turns Smaug's drawback into a life engine
synergies.description: Smaug's trigger is mandatory and costs one life per Treasure-cast spell. Sheoldred, the Apocalypse reads "Whenever you draw a card, you gain 2 life", so the same spell that costs one life now gains two. Every Treasure-cast spell is worth one net life instead of minus one, which turns ten such spells from minus ten life into plus ten. Sheoldred also taxes the table: under the vanilla four-player model each opponent draws once per turn, so her second clause removes two life from each of the three opponents over a turn cycle, six life in total, before any extra draw they take. Without Sheoldred the deck still has no repeatable life gain and plays as a short-clock deck. Warren Soultrader charges one life per activation and Phyrexian Reclamation charges two, so both get much cheaper once she lands. Read the life total as a resource, and prefer the combo line over the grind line when it drops below ten and Sheoldred is not on the battlefield.

synergies.title: Our own sweepers are drain triggers
synergies.description: A board wipe is this deck's worst matchup, so the deck runs three of its own and turns them into reach. Every creature we lose to Blasphemous Act triggers Marionette Apprentice and Pitiless Plunderer, and every Treasure that Plunderer makes triggers Mirkwood Bats. Blasphemous Act costs one generic less for each creature on the battlefield, so in a full board state it costs one red mana. Spiteful Banditry is a scalable X-damage sweeper that also makes us a Treasure when opponents' creatures die, capped at one trigger per turn.

sources.name: Scryfall oracle text
sources.detail: Blasphemous Act, Spiteful Banditry and Marionette Apprentice all verified 2026-08-20.

synergies.title: Beseech the Mirror turns a Treasure into a free combo piece
synergies.description: Beseech the Mirror reads "Bargain (You may sacrifice an artifact, enchantment, or token as you cast this spell.) Search your library for a card, exile it face down, then shuffle. If this spell was bargained, you may cast the exiled card without paying its mana cost if that spell's mana value is 4 or less." This deck makes Treasures, so the bargain cost is free and it also triggers Mirkwood Bats. Ashnod's Altar is mana value 3, Pitiless Plunderer is 4 and Krark-Clan Ironworks is 4, so all three can be found and cast for nothing off a single Beseech.

sources.name: Scryfall oracle text
sources.detail: Beseech the Mirror verified 2026-08-20. Mana values read from the same lookup.

synergies.title: Storm-Kiln Artist doubles as a ritual on the deck twenty-one spells
synergies.description: Storm-Kiln Artist reads "Magecraft — Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, create a Treasure token." The deck runs twenty-one instants and sorceries, so the trigger is live on a third of the nonland cards. Each Treasure it makes is mana for the next spell, a Smaug cast trigger on that spell, and an artifact entering for Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent. It also grows: it reads "gets +1/+0 for each artifact you control", so on a board of ten artifacts it attacks as a 12/2.

highlights.name: Smaug, Wicked Worm
highlights.reason: The commander. Its cast trigger fires once per spell that used Treasure mana, so the deck is built around casting many cheap spells rather than a few large ones. It is a card-advantage engine, not a win condition.

sources.name: Scryfall oracle text
sources.detail: Verified 2026-08-20.

highlights.name: Pitiless Plunderer
highlights.reason: The hinge of the deterministic kill. It turns every creature death into a Treasure, which is both mana and a payoff trigger. Owned in the free pool, so the primary combo costs nothing to assemble.

highlights.name: Ashnod's Altar
highlights.reason: The only free sacrifice outlet in the deck that adds more mana than the Treasure it consumes. That surplus is what makes the loop mana-positive. Krark-Clan Ironworks does the same job for artifacts.

sources.name: CEO analysis
sources.detail: Loop arithmetic derived from verified oracle text.

highlights.name: Xorn
highlights.reason: Every Treasure instruction produces one extra Treasure. In a deck where a Treasure deals damage entering and drains leaving, that is two extra points of reach per instruction before any multiplication from Academy Manufactor. EDHREC inclusion 73 percent.

highlights.name: Mirkwood Bats
highlights.reason: The only payoff that fires on both halves of a token's life. Its text is "Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses 1 life." A single Treasure that is made and then spent drains two from each opponent. EDHREC inclusion 77 percent.

highlights.name: Mayhem Devil
highlights.reason: The bridge payoff. It triggers on "a player sacrifices a permanent," so it fires on our Treasures, on our creatures, and on opponents' fetch lands. It is also the cheapest way to point the infinite loop at a face.

sources.name: EDHREC — Smaug, Wicked Worm
sources.detail: 1,232 of 1,789 decks, 69 percent.

highlights.name: Krark-Clan Ironworks
highlights.reason: The single card that lifts this list above the reference decks. It is a free, unbounded artifact sacrifice outlet that turns each Treasure into two mana instead of one. Neither reference list ran a free outlet, which is the main reason both are Bracket 3.

sources.name: CEO strategy analysis revision 2
sources.detail: Section 5, reason 1.

highlights.name: Marionette Master
highlights.reason: Fabricate 3 makes it a four-power body, and each artifact we lose then drains one opponent for four. Scryfall's ruling confirms Treasure tokens count: artifact tokens reach the graveyard before ceasing to exist, so the trigger fires.

sources.name: Scryfall ruling on Marionette Master
sources.detail: "Artifact tokens that are sacrificed or destroyed are put into their owner's graveyard before ceasing to exist. If you controlled the token, Marionette Master's last ability will trigger."

highlights.name: Deflecting Swat
highlights.reason: Free protection while Smaug is on the battlefield. Bracket philosophy names it as the mandatory red free spell at Bracket 4. Held in the free pool, so its high market price costs the build nothing.

sources.name: data/bracket-philosophy.md
sources.detail: Free-spell requirement for Bracket 4.

highlights.name: Hellkite Tyrant
highlights.reason: Alternate win at twenty artifacts at our upkeep, and a two-card win alongside Mycosynth Lattice because Lattice makes every permanent we control count toward the check. Also steals an opposing artifact board on connection.

highlights.name: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
highlights.reason: The single card that changes how this deck plays. Smaug's cast trigger draws a card and costs one life; Sheoldred gains two on every draw, so each Treasure-cast spell nets one life instead of costing one. She also removes two life from each opponent on their draw step, which is six life across a turn cycle in a four-player game. A 4/5 deathtouch body blocks the creature decks this list otherwise races.
